procedure.method: Fresh independent critic session; no spawn, fork, resume or peer-review inspection. Verified all 33 permitted pins. Read the complete literal packet/case, rules, rubric, compact addendum/method, adapter and ratio policy, then all five pinned native-evidence manifests without following their embedded production paths. The packet declares no source assets or protected-layout manifests, so no source opens or protected-layout reads occurred. Used functions.exec with tools.view_image(detail=original), forwarding each returned image for actual visual inspection. Opened M1 native/usage720/thumbnail320, then M2, M3, M4 and M5 in the same three-view order: all 15 exact views preceded the first deliberate copy-reading/transcription, mandatory judgment, image score or diversity score. First reads were manually transcribed from visible pixels and retained unchanged. Subsequently made exactly one native revisit for each member's ambiguous time-range dash, recorded in its copy entry. Actual poster opens total 20: 15 initial views and 5 native ambiguity revisits; no substitutes, crops or generated views. Scores judge visible construction and readability at the pinned native, 720-by-405 usage and 320-by-180 thumbnail scales. All native dimensions are 1672 by 941; 16:9 uses the predeclared single-edge rounding allowance, since abs(941 - 1672*9/16) is 0.5 pixel rather than zero.

Literal mandatory client conditions:
Print every supplied entry exactly once, with readable Korean/English and intact punctuation; no added text, logos, pseudo-print, watermark or QR.
Each result is one separate flat opaque landscape16:9 poster, not a stretched/cropped portrait or a contact sheet.
Five genuinely distinct complete visual systems, composition, image/type roles and impressions, beyond material/filter/palette changes.
Substantive content-grounded nonglyph visual construction required; type/whitespace-only, tiny icon/texture and glyph-model-only loopholes prohibited.
Outdoor short-film screening and conversation must be recognizable, with an approachable adult cultural-event tone. All supplied practical information must be readable at usage720.

evidence.location: left projector, center lime beam and right screen/audience
evidence.observation: A large foreground film projector casts a graphic beam toward a screen under the bridge; mat-seated viewers and a microphone speaker supply a substantial cinema-and-conversation scene.

evidence.location: left projector, center lime beam and right screen/audience
evidence.observation: A large foreground film projector casts a graphic beam toward a screen under the bridge; mat-seated viewers and a microphone speaker supply a substantial cinema-and-conversation scene.

content_form.location: projector, luminous screen and microphone speaker
content_form.observation: Projection becomes the information vehicle, and the foreground viewers and speaker connect the device to both the film and conversation activities. The nonglyph scene does substantial communicative work.

hierarchy.observation: The title establishes the event, the lime beam directs the eye to the prominent time and schedule, and the rule separates primary information from participation details.
The major title/time relationship survives reduction, while foreground equipment clearly establishes cinema. Small logistics lose prominence but do not alter the main sequence.

typography.location: two small columns at bottom of the lime screen
typography.observation: Admission, mat, free-entry and weather text is legible in the static usage image but has much smaller letter height than the large schedule. Tight placement in two columns and the screen perspective make these practical instructions demand close attention for the intended public display.
The small logistics compress into dense dark lines while the enormous title and time remain highly legible; the type system does not retain balanced support across scales.
The time bar was resolved as a visual en dash in the single native revisit; glyph fidelity itself is not the reason for the low rating.

space.observation: The widening beam links the foreground lens to the slanted screen, and the large title uses the remaining dark upper-left field. A horizontal rule and central divider organize the compact lower instructions.
The foreground group grounds the image without covering the information-bearing screen surface.

image_material.location: projector housing, bridge structure and halftone surfaces
image_material.observation: Halftone texture, orange edges and purple shadows are carried consistently across machinery, bridge and audience. The projection wedge is deliberately graphic rather than a photographic light simulation, but its origin and destination remain readable.
The frame has visible supports, and the speaker's microphone and stance remain recognizable against the lime ground.

emotion_control.location: lime projection against purple/orange evening scene
emotion_control.observation: The energized contrast communicates a lively film occasion without losing the small seated neighborhood audience. The adults on mats and conversational speaker keep the tone accessible.

ai_slop.location: projector lens, projection wedge and screen boundary
ai_slop.observation: The large constructed parts have a clear causal image relationship; the halftone is consistent and no arbitrary icon scatter or pseudo-lettering fills the image. The compact equipment details are stylized but remain subordinate to the recognizable projector.

residuals: Practical instructions below the screen rule are too small relative to the emphatic title/time for equally confident public-display reading, despite being readable at usage720.
The lime/peach-purple contrast and heavy two-line title repeat M2's visual vocabulary.

layout.observations: Upper-right English line, with visibly expanded letter spacing.
Left-column single line beneath the red time.

transcriptions.ambiguity: The first visual reading is a horizontal time-range dash, but its glyph class (en dash versus hyphen-minus) is uncertain; width alone depends on the unknown font.

revisit.reason: One exact native revisit to distinguish the visible time-range dash class after the first read; no replacement or crop.
revisit.resolution: The native red time line shows an extended bar nearly the ink width of the neighboring zero, rather than a short hyphen. The visible glyph is read as an en dash.

ambiguities.description: The first visual reading is a horizontal time-range dash, but its glyph class (en dash versus hyphen-minus) is uncertain; width alone depends on the unknown font.

evidence.location: lower-right event scene and large left schedule
evidence.observation: Outdoor screening, mat seating and a microphone discussion are recognizable under a substantial bridge. A warm photographic gathering, neutral ground and restrained red schedule convey an approachable adult event.

evidence.location: left practical column and upper-right title
evidence.observation: All ten strings appear once and remain readable. Date and time lead, with event description, location, entry, free-entry, mat and weather lines below; the title and English name occupy the right. No other readable copy, logo, QR or watermark is visible.

evidence.location: whole canvas
evidence.observation: One flat opaque landscape poster fills native 1672 by 941, with the declared 16:9 condition met by allowed 0.5-pixel height rounding rather than exact equality.

evidence.location: composition relative to all members
evidence.observation: The schedule-first left column, upper-right title and lower-right photo fading into a light field reverse M1's image/sidebar emphasis; they also differ from M2's portraits, M3's full illustration and M4's screen-bound type. The shared photographic bridge scene with M1 limits novelty but the information structure changes.

evidence.location: lower-right bridge screening and discussion scene
evidence.observation: A substantial bridge-and-river scene contains a projector, screen, mat-seated adult audience and a microphone speaker with seated panel/listeners, so the image is more than type and an ornament.

evidence.location: lower-right bridge screening and discussion scene
evidence.observation: A substantial bridge-and-river scene contains a projector, screen, mat-seated adult audience and a microphone speaker with seated panel/listeners, so the image is more than type and an ornament.

content_form.location: lower-right audience, projector and discussion group
content_form.observation: The screen, mats and speaker/panel show both components of the event in an identifiable outdoor bridge setting; the scene is large enough to communicate independently of the text.

hierarchy.location: upper-left red schedule, right title and left details
hierarchy.observation: Red date/time provides a deliberate participation-first entry; the large title remains separately findable at upper right, and the practical left column descends in a clear linear path.
Date/time and event title remain the primary signals, with the bridge image supplying contextual recognition even after figure detail reduces.

typography.location: left column and upper-right English name
typography.observation: Hangul forms, date punctuation and word gaps are stable; the English name has deliberate expanded tracking that stays within one line. The two-line title wrap does not change the words.
The larger supporting type retains readable entry, free-entry, mat and weather lines. The time bar was resolved by one native revisit.

space.location: left text column and upper-right title
space.observation: Consistent left edges and generous row spacing organize the practical details; the right title has its own upper margin, and the bridge diagonal connects that area to the lower image.
The photo keeps the screen and audience visible beneath the title rather than filling the entire ground, making room for a clean schedule field.

image_material.location: left edge of the photographic scene at stairs, shrubs and mats
image_material.observation: The scene changes into the light background through uneven feathering and partly cut shrub/stair contours, while nearby bridge and screen edges stay crisp. The inconsistent transition gives the composite a less finished boundary.

image_material.location: bridge, warm lighting and viewing area
image_material.observation: The main bridge and cinema scene are coherent, but the image-to-ground integration is less precise than the solid photo/panel division in M1.

emotion_control.location: warm lower-right scene and quiet neutral field
emotion_control.observation: A modest adult audience, amber illumination and generous light ground make the event calm and welcoming; the red schedule adds practical urgency without turning it into an alarm-like notice.

ai_slop.observation: The event apparatus and audience are recognizable, and the main architecture has a consistent bridge setting. No arbitrary decorative badges or pseudo-print are visible; the rough transition is a compositing finish issue located in image_material rather than an invented object failure.

residuals: The irregular feathered photograph boundary at the left of the stairs and shrubs remains visibly less resolved.
The scene shares M1's familiar bridge/screen/audience imagery; the schedule-first layout supplies most of its distinction.
Discussion participants become small at usage720 and are primarily contextual at thumbnail320.

recording_adapter.limit: Metadata bindings and attestations do not prove semantic viewing or source fidelity

evidence.location: full photograph plus right panel
evidence.observation: A broad documentary view with title over sky and a fixed right practical column establishes an image-first notice. It differs from M5's left schedule-first field and lower-right cutout, and from the montage, illustrated panorama and integrated-screen type in M2–M4.

evidence.location: opposing faces, central title and angled cards
evidence.observation: A conversation-centered portrait montage uses two enormous faces as a frame for the event name, with information in opposing angular corners and a smaller screening scene below. M4 shares its purple/peach/lime vocabulary, but its projection apparatus, viewpoint and screen-bound copy create a different composition and image/type role.

evidence.location: continuous river, diagonal bridge and two banks
evidence.observation: An overhead illustrated panorama connects separately staged screening and dialogue across the river. Information is spread into bank openings rather than placed in M1/M5 columns, M2 cards or M4's screen. Its small scene scale and narrative viewpoint materially change the impression.

evidence.location: projector-to-screen beam and information surface
evidence.observation: A close foreground projector sends a strong wedge across the image, and the screen carries the time, place and instructions. Compared with M2's face-led collage, the device and projection geometry control the composition; compared with M1/M5, type is part of the scene rather than an independent plain panel.

evidence.location: red left schedule, upper-right identity and lower-right scene
evidence.observation: A light-ground composition begins with date/time, runs practical copy down the left and places title above a smaller bridge scene at right. It shares photographic local-cinema content with M1, but changes the dominant information, crop, image scale and occupied/empty-space relationships.

evidence.location: central title in relation to M4 title
evidence.observation: M2 and M4 both use a very heavy two-line Korean title, prominent English line, purple ground and lime/peach accents. This is a real family resemblance, so the set earns strong diversity rather than exceptional diversity; differences are grounded in composition and functional roles, not just material names.

evidence.location: title and practical panel compared with all five
evidence.observation: Every member uses heavy sans-serif Hangul and a readily identified cinema scene. The set varies layout, viewpoint, activity emphasis and information-bearing surfaces enough for five distinct systems, while typographic breadth remains narrower than its compositional breadth.

residuals: M2 and M4 share purple/peach/lime color relationships and a heavy two-line title with English beneath.
M1 and M5 both rely on a photographic bridge, screen and seated audience; their strongest difference is the schedule/identity hierarchy and image-panel relationship.
Heavy sans-serif typography recurs throughout the set; none of the five introduces a markedly different type voice.
The below-4 individual craft findings are retained in M3 hierarchy/space, M4 typography and M5 image_material; set diversity does not cancel them.
This is one independent craft review of the pinned five-member version; it does not establish other critics' judgments, real-device viewing or performance on unseen requests.
